plain_description.what: Keeps the tree's declared top two levels fixed and replaces the splitting rule below them with alternatives: plain spherical k-means, a PCA plus Gaussian mixture, and k-means that knows the class labels. It compares how well each one files held-out questions. No judge calls.
plain_description.why: An earlier test found the tree lost to label-aware k-means below depth 2. This one asks whether the cause is the splitting rule or the label information.
plain_description.information: If a label-free rule closes the gap, the engine's splitting rule should change. If only label-aware k-means does, the gap comes from labels and changing the engine is not worth it. Result: done. Plain k-means files worse than the tree's own rule (by a thin margin, one construction). Label-aware k-means files better than plain k-means. No label-free rule recovers half the gap, so the splitting rule is not the cause. A descriptive check places the edge in which items enter the depth-2 fit, not in labels below depth 2.
